questions.stem: The Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), a premier national film school under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, is located in which city?

options.option_text: Mumbai, the headquarters of the Bollywood industry
Pune, set up on the former Prabhat Film Company premises
Chennai, home of the South Indian Tamil film industry
Hyderabad, a major centre for Telugu-language cinema

questions.explanation: FTII is located in Pune, Maharashtra, on the historic premises of the Prabhat Film Company studio established in 1934. It was set up in 1960 under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Mumbai is the most common wrong answer because it hosts Bollywood, but FTII was deliberately placed in Pune to utilise the existing studio infrastructure of Prabhat Films.

questions.stem: The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC), which grants 'U', 'A', 'UA' and 'S' certificates to films before public exhibition in India, is headquartered in which city?

options.option_text: New Delhi, seat of the Union Government ministries
Chennai, heart of the South Indian film industries
Mumbai, Maharashtra, where the main CBFC office is based
Kolkata, West Bengal, the early cradle of Indian cinema

questions.explanation: The CBFC (popularly called the Censor Board) is headquartered in Mumbai, established under the Cinematograph Act, 1952. New Delhi is the most tempting wrong answer because it houses the parent Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, but the CBFC's main operational office is in Mumbai, with regional offices in other cities.

questions.stem: The 'Golden Peacock' trophy for Best Film is the top prize at which major international film festival held annually in India?

options.option_text: Kolkata International Film Festival, founded in 1995
Mumbai International Film Festival, held since 1990
International Film Festival of India (IFFI), held at Goa
Kerala International Film Festival, held in Thiruvananthapuram

questions.explanation: The Golden Peacock is awarded at IFFI (International Film Festival of India), held in Panaji, Goa, and is one of the oldest and most prestigious film festivals in Asia, recognised by FIAPF. The Kolkata International Film Festival is a common wrong pick, but its top award is the Golden Royal Bengal Tiger, not the Golden Peacock.

questions.stem: The Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI), India's second national film school established by the Government of India in 1995, is located in which city?

options.option_text: Pune, Maharashtra, adjacent to the FTII main campus
Mumbai, Maharashtra, in the Andheri film production belt
Kolkata, West Bengal, in the East Kolkata township area
Bengaluru, Karnataka, near the Chitrakala Parishath

questions.explanation: SRFTI is located in Kolkata, West Bengal, and was established in 1995 under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, named after the legendary filmmaker Satyajit Ray. Pune is the most common wrong answer because candidates know FTII is there — the key distinction is that India has two national film institutes: FTII in Pune and SRFTI in Kolkata.

questions.stem: At the 1956 Cannes Film Festival, Satyajit Ray's 'Pather Panchali' became India's first film to win a major international prize at Cannes. By what name was that award known?

options.option_text: Jury Prize for Best Film from the Asian continent
Best Human Document (Prix du document humain) award
Palme d'Or, the highest honour at the Cannes festival
FIPRESCI Prize awarded by the international film critics

questions.explanation: Pather Panchali (1955) won the 'Best Human Document' (Prix du document humain) — a special award created by the jury — at Cannes 1956 for its compassionate portrayal of rural Bengal life. The Palme d'Or is the most tempting wrong answer since it is Cannes' supreme prize, but Pather Panchali did not win that; it received a specially constituted jury award recognising the film's humanist depth.

questions.stem: 'Bhuvan Shome' (1969), widely regarded as the film that launched the Indian New Wave (parallel cinema) movement, was directed by which filmmaker?

options.option_text: Ritwik Ghatak, celebrated for his Bengal partition trilogy
Shyam Benegal, known for the social-realist film Ankur (1974)
Mrinal Sen, a National Award-winning parallel cinema director
Adoor Gopalakrishnan, pioneer of Malayalam parallel cinema

questions.explanation: Bhuvan Shome (1969) was directed by Mrinal Sen and is widely considered the film that sparked India's New Wave parallel cinema movement; it was financed by the Film Finance Corporation (FFC) and broke conventional narrative norms. Ritwik Ghatak is the most tempting distractor since he is also a towering figure of the era, but his major works (Meghe Dhaka Tara, Subarnarekha) predate Bhuvan Shome and Ghatak is not credited with defining the 'New Wave' label the way Mrinal Sen's film is.

questions.stem: J. C. Daniel is historically recognised as the 'Father of Malayalam Cinema'. Which film, self-financed by Daniel, is cited as the first Malayalam feature film?

options.option_text: Neelakuyil (1954), the first widely acclaimed Malayalam sound film
Jeevitha Nauka (1951), a noted early Malayalam narrative film
Vigathakumaran (1928), considered the first Malayalam silent film
Balan (1938), regarded as the first full-length Malayalam talkie

questions.explanation: J. C. Daniel directed and self-financed Vigathakumaran (1928), recognised as the first Malayalam feature film, after which he suffered financial ruin and remained forgotten for decades before being rediscovered. Balan (1938) is the sharpest distractor because it is indeed the first Malayalam talkie — but that was directed by S. Notani, not J. C. Daniel, whose historic contribution belongs to the silent era of 1928.
